column1: # Objective-C type encodings (armv7) for the Apple framework selectors that
# 32-bit games send. Used when a guest message reaches a host (64-bit)
# framework object, whose methods carry no encodings.
# How the list was made (2026-10-22): for each 32-bit game, the selectors in
# __objc_selrefs minus every selector the game's own classes and categories
# both lists merged and sorted. Selectors a game implements need no row: the
# game's own method types are used. Encodings follow Apple's SDK headers for
# float, BOOL signed char ('c'), NSTimeInterval double. Stack offsets are left
# Columns: selector, encoding (return type, then self, _cmd, arguments),
#   format       the last fixed argument is a printf-style format and
#                variadic arguments follow (read by the format);
#   nil-list     variadic object arguments follow, ended by nil;
#   ambiguous    classes disagree on the types; the encoding is for the
#                class the games use (named after the colon);
#   float        the row's scalar 'f' arguments are C float on the 64-bit
#                side too (without it a scalar 'f' is CGFloat: double there).
#                UIEdgeInsets are always CGFloat. Float returns need no
#                mark: the host's return register tells float from double.
#   in-array     id-pointer arguments are arrays of as many ids as the last
#                integer argument says, read before the call;
#   out-array    the same, filled by the host (not read first).
# Several notes are separated by commas.
# A selector missing here stops the game with its name when a framework
# NSObject basics: a game may implement these too (so the derivation above
# leaves them out), but they still reach Apple's classes through super and
# through the game's own classes' framework roots.
